---
title: How to brew green tea
lang: en
free: true
---

Green tea is easy to ruin and easy to get right once you respect the temperature. Unlike black tea, its delicate leaves turn bitter in water that is too hot.

## Water temperature

Aim for water around 70–80°C, well below boiling. If your kettle only boils, let it stand for a couple of minutes first. Hot-but-not-boiling water draws out the sweet, grassy notes while leaving the harsh tannins behind.

## Steeping

Use a teaspoon of leaves per cup and steep for only one to two minutes. Taste early — green tea is forgiving if you stop in time and punishing if you forget it. Good leaves can be steeped two or three more times, and many people find the second infusion the best.

Serve it without milk or sugar so the subtle flavour comes through.
